channel.title: Interesting Engineering – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Interesting Engineering – Bias and Credibility (interestingengineering.com)

item.title: Renault to use humanoid robots for logistics, heavy tasks in factories
item.description: Renault plans to deploy 350 Calvin humanoid robots across factories to handle material movement and repetitive industrial tasks in actories.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg building AI agent to assist with Meta CEO role: Report
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg is testing an AI agent designed to assist with CEO responsibilities, highlighting AI's expanding role in decision-making.

item.title: AeroVironment to supply jam-resistant attack drones to US Army
item.description: The U.S. Army has awarded a $17.58 million contract to defense company, AeroVironment, for the procurement of Red Dragon, a one-way attack drone.

item.title: First Black Hawk that can fly without pilot delivered to US Army
item.description: The U.S. Army has received its first H-60Mx Black Hawk, a modified helicopter that can fly with or without a pilot.

item.title: US students design quadrotor biplane for lifesaving missions
item.description: The quadrotor biplane will be used for emergency tasks, including delivering medical supplies, and locating trapped individuals.

item.title: Lockheed SPY-7 radar passes live target tracking test for Japan ships
item.description: The U.S. Missile Defense Agency has completed the first live-target tracking test of the SPY-7 radar, clearing a key hurdle for Japan's ASEV program.

item.title: New method checks heat exchanger strength for safer nuclear reactors
item.description: A new method helps verify diffusion weld strength, boosting confidence in compact heat exchangers for next-gen nuclear reactors.

item.title: Europe's largest vanadium flow battery stores 8 MWh for over 15 hours
item.description: Spain has just completed testing Europe's biggest vanadium battery with more than 15 hours of energy storage.

item.title: 36 years later, sunken Soviet nuclear sub still leaks radiation
item.description: Researchers detected a visible plume of radioactive material escaping from a ventilation pipe near the reactor compartment.

item.title: Exoskeletons field tested by Ukrainian artillery reducing reload time
item.description: Ukrainian troops are testing lightweight exoskeletons that fit in a briefcase, helping artillery crews carry heavy shells and reduce fatigue.
